title: An optimized protocol for high-throughput amplicon-based microbiome profiling
protocol: Vortex samples to mix at 1900 RPM for 15 seconds and spin-down on centrifuge.

Using the Liquidator or a multichannel pipet, dispense 10 μl of undiluted sample into quadrant 1 (A01) of a 384-well deep-well plate that already has 18 μl water dispensed into quadrants 2 (A02), 3 (B01), and 4 (B02).
Label plate appropriately.
Make a 10-fold dilution series using one set of 20 μl Liquidator tips or a multichannel pipet.
Transfer 2 μl of each sample from quadrant 1 (A01) to quadrant 2 (A02).
Mix by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Do not go to the second stop on the Liquidator trigger to avoid introducing bubbles.
Using the same tips, transfer 2 μl of well-mixed sample from quadrant 2 (A02) to quadrant 3 (B01).
Mix samples in quadrant 3 by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Transfer well-mixed samples from quadrant 3 (B01) to quadrant 4 (B02) to complete the dilution series.
Change the volume on the Liquidator to 3 μl.
Transfer 3 μl of each dilution to a barcoded 384-well PCR plate, starting with the most dilute sample in quadrant 4 (B02).
End by transferring the most concentrated sample from quadrant 1 (A01) to the plate.
Label the plate appropriately.
Cover the plate with a foil seal.
Vortex the plate to mix and spin down on a centrifuge.
Store plates at -20°C or continue to primary PCR.
Thaw KAPA HiFi PCR kit reagents as well as the sample dilution 384-well plate if stored in freezer.
Vortex and centrifuge the plate(s) and reagents before use.
Make a 2x KAPA HiFi qPCR master mix using the following recipe: 1.2 µl of 5x KAPA HiFi buffer, 0.18 µl of 10 mM dNTPs, 0.3 µl DMSO, and 0.12 µl ROX (25 µM).
Mix 0.3 µl of forward primer (10 µM).
Mix 0.3 µl of reverse primer (10 µM).
Add 0.48 µl of nuclease-free water.
Pipette 3 μl of 2x KAPA HiFi qPCR master mix into each reaction well on the 384-well plate.
Seal the plate with an optical seal.
Vortex the plate at 1900 rpm for 15 seconds to mix.
Spin down the plate in a centrifuge.
Run the following qPCR protocol: start with 95°C for 5 minutes, then cycle 15-30 times of 98°C for 20 seconds, 55°C for 15 seconds, and 72°C for 1 minute. End with a hold at 4°C.
Store the plate at -20°C or proceed to analysis and cherry-picking followed by primary PCR dilution.
Export the “Clipped data” .txt file from the ABI 7900.
Open the exported file with Microsoft Excel.
Paste the contents of the file into the “paste clipped data” tab of the DI_qPCR_Analysis.xlsx template.
Examine the amplification curves for each sample in the “96-well summary” tab of the DI_qPCR_Analysis.xlsx spreadsheet.
Enter the number of amplification cycles and a target Rn value in the “Set thresholds” tab.
Minimize the selection of plateaued samples by entering “TRUE” in the “Exclude overamplified samples?” box on the “Set thresholds” tab.
Double-check the cherry-picking choices in the “Calculations” tab.
Save the data in the “EpMotion program” tab as a .csv file.
Centrifuge the 384-well qPCR plate to collect sample and remove the optical seal from the plate.
Transfer 2 μl of sample of the appropriate dilution from the 384-well qPCR plate to a 96-well plate containing 18 μl of water, making a 1:10 dilution of the initial PCR.
Cover 1:10 dilution plate with foil seal, vortex at 1900 RPM for 30 seconds and spin down in centrifuge.
Transfer 5 μl of the sample to a 96-well plate containing 45 μl of water to make a 1:100 dilution.
Store plates at -20°C or continue on to Indexing PCR.
Normalize samples to a consistent concentration in a 96-well plate if desired.
Transfer 3 ul of sample from each well to a 96-well run plate.
Seal the plate with a foil seal.
Vortex samples to mix at 1900RPM for 15 seconds and spin-down in a centrifuge.
Thaw the KAPA HiFi PCR kit reagents as well as 96-well plate if it has been stored in the freezer.
Vortex and centrifuge the plate(s) and reagents when thawed before use.

Make a 2x KAPA HiFi PCR master mix using: 1.2 µl of 5x KAPA HiFi buffer, 0.18 µl of 10 mM dNTPs, 0.3 µl DMSO, 0.12 µl KAPA HiFi Polymerase, 0.3 µl forward primer (10 µM), 0.3 µl reverse primer (10 µM), and 0.6 µl nuclease-free water.
Dispense 3 μl of the 2x KAPA HiFi PCR master mix in each reaction well on a 96-well plate containing sample for a final volume of 6 μl.
Seal the plates with Microseal PCR film.
Vortex at 1900 rpm for 15 seconds to mix and spin down in centrifuge.
Run the following PCR protocol: Start with 95°C for 5 minutes, then proceed with 15-30 cycles of 98°C for 20 seconds.
Transfer 2 μl of sample from each well of the 96-well Primary PCR plate to a new plate containing 18 μl of water, making a 1:10 dilution of the initial PCR.
Cover the 1:10 dilution plate with foil seal.
Vortex the covered plate at 1900 RPM for 30 seconds and spin down in centrifuge.
Transfer 5 μl of the sample to another new plate containing 45 μl of water to make a 1:100 dilution.
Label both dilution plates appropriately.
Determine an i5 and i7 dual-indexing scheme, ensuring no index overlap between samples to be pooled for sequencing.
Thaw the KAPA HiFi PCR kit reagents and Primary PCR 1:100 dilution plate if stored in the freezer.
Vortex and centrifuge the thawed plates and reagents before use.
Ensure there is a corresponding 5 μM oligo plate for each index scheme being used.
Make a 3.33x KAPA HiFi Indexing PCR master mix using the specified recipe.
Dispense 3 ul of the master mix into each well of a 96-well PCR plate.
Label the PCR plate appropriately.
Pull 5 μl from the Primary PCR 1:100 dilution plate and dispense into the corresponding wells in the PCR plate containing the master mix.
Pull 2 μl from the appropriate 5 μM indexing scheme plate and add to the corresponding wells in the PCR plate.
Draw up 10 μl reaction dispense into a 384-well plate starting in quadrant 1, A01.
Label the PCR plate appropriately.
Repeat steps using a new set of Liquidator tips if there is more than one plate to set up.
Cover the PCR plate with Microseal PCR film.
Vortex the covered PCR plate at 1900 RPM for 30 seconds.
Spin down the PCR plate in a centrifuge.
Amplify the PCR plate for 10 cycles on the BioRad Tetrad using cycling conditions: 95°C – 5 minutes, followed by 10 cycles of 98°C – 20 seconds, 55°C – 15 seconds, and 72°C – 1 minute.
Hold the PCR plate at 4°C after amplification.
Centrifuge the PCR plate to collect the sample after the program is complete.
Determine individual sample concentrations using PicoGreen.
Determine a desired concentration for normalization.
Calculate the amount of water needed for each sample to achieve the desired concentration.
Transfer the appropriate amount of water to each well of a new 96-well plate using an EpMotion.
Label the 96-well plate appropriately.
Add a fixed volume of indexing PCR sample to each well on the normalization plate using a Liquidator or multichannel pipette.
Cover the plate with foil.
Vortex the plate to mix thoroughly.
Spin down the plate in the centrifuge.
Dispense an equal volume of each sample into a trough.
Mix well and transfer from the trough to a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Use the Speedvac to concentrate the sample pool down to 20-100 μl.
Purify the concentrated sample using 1X AmPureXP beads.
If doing size selection on the Caliper XT, elute in 12.5 μl of nuclease-free water.
If not size selecting or if pooling more than 1.5 μg of sample, elute in 25 μl of nuclease-free water or EB.
Store samples at -20°C or continue to Library QC.
Purify the 10 μl indexing PCR reactions using a SequalPrep normalization plate following manufacturer’s instructions.
Assess sufficient input material post-indexing PCR for new sample types using the PicoGreen assay.
Dispense 10 μl of each sample to be pooled into a trough.
Mix well and transfer from the trough to a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Concentrate the sample pool down to 20-100 μl using a Speedvac.
Purify the concentrated sample pool using 1X AmPureXP beads.
Elute the purified sample in 25 μl of nuclease-free water or EB (10 mM Tris-Cl, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0).
Store samples at -20°C or proceed to Library QC.
Remove Caliper LabChip XT DNA 750 kit reagents and AmPureXP beads from the 4°C storage and allow them to reach room temperature.
Load 10 μl of the concentrated pool on a single Caliper LabChip DNA 750 chip lane.
Cut depending on the region being amplified, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Do not overload the chip (> 1 μg) as this can affect DNA migration and accuracy of sizing.
Purify sample with 1.8X AmPureXP Beads and elute in 20 μl of water.
Store samples at -20°C or continue to library QC.
Perform library QC by running pooled library on an Agilent DNA HS chip, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Determine the concentration of the pooled library by PicoGreen (following manufacturer’s protocol).
Dilute the pooled library to 2 nM in EB using the concentration determined by the PicoGreen assay and the expected size for the amplicon.
Thaw MiSeq reagent kit (typically either a 500 cycle v2 or 600 cycle v3 kit).
Generate a MiSeq sample sheet using the Illumina Experiment Manager program and paste in the sample and barcode information.
Load the sample sheet on the MiSeq.
Follow Illumina’s protocol for preparing the instrument and flow cell.
In a 1.5 ml microfuge tube, incubate 10 μl of 2 nM library with freshly diluted 0.2 N NaOH for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add 980 μl of Illumina’s HT1 buffer to bring the sample to 20 pM.
Mix 400 μl of 20 pM library and 600 μl of Illumina’s HT1 buffer in a clean 1.5 ml microfuge tube to dilute to 8 pM.
Prepare 8 pM PhiX.
Remove 150 μl of the 8 pM library and discard.
Add 150 μl of 8 pM PhiX to the remaining 850 μl of 8 pM library (15% PhiX spike).
Add 600 μl of the 8 pM (15% PhiX) library to the sample well of the MiSeq cartridge and initiate sequencing.
Make 10 μM daughter plates containing desired forward and reverse indexing schemes from the 100 μM stock plates.
Add 270 μl of nuclease-free water to each well of the column corresponding to the indices for the forward indexing scheme in a deep-well 96-well plate.
Transfer 30 μl of each forward index to the columns containing water in the deep-well plate.
Add 180 μl of nuclease-free water to each well of the row corresponding to the indices for the reverse indexing scheme in another deep-well 96-well plate.
Transfer 20 μl of each reverse index to the rows containing water in the deep-well plate.
Using a multichannel pipet, add 20 μl of the 10 μM forward primers column-wise to a new 96-well plate.
Label the plate appropriately with the indexing scheme identifier (e.g., Indexing scheme 1B).
Using a multichannel pipet, add 20 μl of the 10 μM reverse primers row-wise to the 96-well plate containing forward primers.
Using a multichannel pipet or the liquidator, add 40 μl of water to each well to create a 5 μM master plate containing 80 μl of indexing primer mix.
Seal the plate with a foil seal.
Vortex the plate at 1900 rpm for 15 seconds to mix.
Spin-down the plate in a centrifuge.
Thaw the indexing scheme master plate if it has been stored in the freezer.
Vortex and centrifuge the plate when thawed before using it.
Carefully remove the foil seal from the indexing scheme master plate.
Use the liquidator or a multichannel pipet to dispense 12 μl of primer mix from each well into each of 6 96-well plates.
Store indexing scheme plates at -20°C.
Add appropriate volume of well-mixed AmPure XP beads using a multichannel pipette to each well if using a plate-based magnet or to each tube if using a tube-based magnet.
Allow the sample and beads to incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Place the plate or tubes on the magnetic stand at room temperature for 2 minutes, until the liquid appears clear.
Remove and discard the supernatant, being careful not to disturb the magnetic bead pellet.
With the magnetic plate still on the stand, wash the bead pellet 2X for 30 seconds with 200-500 μl of fresh 80% ethanol while not disturbing the pellet.
Make sure that 80% ethanol completely covers the beads during the wash.
Remove all traces of the 80% ethanol and let the plate/tubes dry at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the beads in designated amount of nuclease free water and pipette gently to mix.
Allow beads/sample to incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Place the plate/tubes back on the magnetic stand at room temperature for 2 minutes, until the liquid appears clear.
Transfer supernatant containing the eluted DNA to a new tube or plate.
